mcq.s: Which of the following is not a measure of selective credit control?
mcq.x: Sale or purchase of government securities (open market operations) is a quantitative (general) credit control tool; lending margins, credit rationing and moral suasion are selective (qualitative) measures.

mcq.s:
Arrange the following Governors of the Reserve Bank of India in chronological order:
I. Dr. C. Rangarajan
II. Dr. I.G. Patel
III. Dr. D. Subbarao
IV. Dr. Manmohan Singh
mcq.x: I.G. Patel (1977-82), Manmohan Singh (1982-85), C. Rangarajan (1992-97) and D. Subbarao (2008-13).

mcq.s: The Negotiable Instruments Act came into effect in:
mcq.x: The Negotiable Instruments Act was passed in December 1881 and came into force on 1 March 1882; it governs cheques, promissory notes and bills of exchange.

why: company law (LLP form of business) not in Group 2 syllabus

mcq.s:
Match the year in List-I with the institution set up in List-II:
List-I
a. 1955
b. 1964
c. 1982
d. 1987
List-II
i. Export-Import Bank of India
ii. Industrial Development Bank of India
iii. Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India
iv. Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
mcq.x: ICICI was formed in 1955, IDBI in 1964, EXIM Bank in 1982 and BIFR was set up in 1987.

why: out of date: FMC merged with SEBI in 2015

mcq.s: Which among the following agencies regulates the mutual funds in India?
mcq.x: Mutual funds are registered with and regulated by SEBI under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996.

why: same fact as gc-econ-7d50e907 added in this job

mcq.s: Which one of the following organisations is the main regulator of stock markets in India?
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
mcq.x: SEBI (statutory since 1992 under the SEBI Act) regulates the securities markets; it replaced the Controller of Capital Issues.

why: same fact as gc-econ-7d50e907 added in this job

mcq.s: Private sector mutual funds in India were permitted in:
mcq.x: Private sector mutual funds entered in 1993, the year the first SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations came in; Kothari Pioneer was the first private fund registered.

mcq.s: The objective of the Unit Trust of India (set up in 1964) was:
o: To give the benefit of its earnings to small investors
To invest in such a way as to promote industrial development
mcq.x: UTI was set up on 1 February 1964 to mobilise the savings of small investors and invest them in industry, passing the earnings back to them.

why: out of date: UTI was largest in 1995; now SBI Mutual Fund

mcq.s: The promoters of the National Stock Exchange of India included:
mcq.x: NSE (set up in 1992 on the Pherwani Committee's recommendation) was promoted by IDBI, SBI, IFCI, LIC, GIC and other financial institutions.

mcq.s: A rise in 'SENSEX' means:
o: a rise in prices of shares of all companies registered with the Bombay Stock Exchange
a rise in prices of shares of all companies registered with the National Stock Exchange
an overall rise in prices of shares of a group of companies registered with the Bombay Stock Exchange
a rise in prices of shares of all companies belonging to a group of companies registered with the Bombay Stock Exchange
mcq.x: SENSEX is a free-float market-capitalisation index of 30 large companies listed on the BSE, so a rise shows an overall rise in the prices of this group of shares.

why: same fact as gc-econ-4960f752 added in this job

mcq.s: How many companies are included in BSE-GREENEX?
mcq.x: BSE GREENEX tracks the top 25 'green' companies from the BSE-100 chosen on greenhouse gas emissions, market cap and liquidity.

mcq.s: The terms 'Bull' and 'Bear' are associated with which branch of commercial activity?
mcq.x: Bulls expect share prices to rise and bears expect them to fall; the terms describe share (stock) market conditions.

mcq.s: In the parlance of financial investments, the term 'bear' denotes:
o: An investor who feels that the price of a particular security is going to fall
An investor who expects the price of particular shares to rise
A shareholder or a bondholder who has an interest in a company, financial or otherwise
Any lender, whether by making a loan or buying a bond
mcq.x: A bear expects prices of securities to fall, so sells them and buys back later at lower prices; a bull expects prices to rise.

mcq.s: Which among the following is not a speculator in the stock exchange?
mcq.x: Bulls, bears, stags and lame ducks are speculators; a broker is an authorised member who trades on clients' behalf for a commission.

mcq.s: Insider trading is related to:
mcq.x: Insider trading is buying or selling a listed company's shares using material non-public information; SEBI prohibits it under its PIT Regulations.

mcq.s: In the context of finance, the term 'beta' refers to:
o: the process of simultaneous buying and selling of an asset from different platforms
an investment strategy of a portfolio manager to balance risk versus reward
a type of systemic risk that arises where perfect hedging is not possible
a numeric value that measures the fluctuations of a stock to changes in the overall stock market
mcq.x: Beta measures a stock's volatility (systematic risk) relative to the market as a whole; a beta above 1 means a more volatile stock.

mcq.s: Capital market means:
mcq.x: The capital market deals in long-term funds through shares, bonds and debentures (primary and secondary markets); short-term funds belong to the money market.

mcq.s: 'Blue Chip' means:
o: Shares listed in the stock exchange
Shares giving consistently high rate of return
mcq.x: Blue chip shares are of large, well-established, financially sound companies with dependable earnings and steady returns.

mcq.s: Sweat equity shares are issued to which of the following?
mcq.x: Sweat equity shares are issued to directors or employees at a discount or for non-cash consideration, for their know-how or value addition.

mcq.s: Which one of the following is irrelevant in the context of the share market?
mcq.x: Sensex, BSE and Nifty relate to the share market; SAPs (Structural Adjustment Programmes) are IMF-World Bank policy conditions for loans.

mcq.s: Debenture holders of a company are its:
mcq.x: A debenture is a debt instrument carrying fixed interest, so debenture holders are creditors of the company, not owners.

mcq.s: In banking transactions, PIN stands for:
mcq.x: A Personal Identification Number is the numeric code entered with a payment card to authenticate a transaction.

mcq.s: Which one of the following is not a prepaid payment instrument?
o: Credit card of a nationalised bank
mcq.x: Metro cards, e-wallets and Airtel Money are loaded in advance (prepaid); a credit card is a post-paid line of credit.

mcq.s: For the existence of a market, which of the following is indispensable?
mcq.x: A market is where goods and services are bought and sold at a price; without prices there is no exchange and so no market.

mcq.s: A buyer's market is one where:
o: supply is more than the demand
demand is more than the supply
demand is equal to the supply
mcq.x: In a buyer's market supply exceeds demand, so buyers have the upper hand in bargaining on price.

why: e-commerce business models (C2B) not in Group 2 syllabus

mcq.s: Which type of market (on the basis of time) is suitable for vegetables?
mcq.x: Perishables like vegetables, fruits and flowers have a fixed supply that cannot be changed at once, so they are traded in a very short period market where price depends on demand.

mcq.s: Supply-side economics lays greater emphasis on the point of view of the:
mcq.x: Supply-side economics holds that production (supply) drives growth and favours tax cuts and incentives for producers and investors.

mcq.s: A consumer is said to be in equilibrium if:
o: he is able to fulfil his needs with a given level of income
he is able to live in full comforts with a given level of income
he can fulfil his needs without consumption of certain goods
he is able to locate new sources of income
mcq.x: A consumer is in equilibrium when he gets the most satisfaction from a given income and gains nothing by changing what he buys (MUx/Px = MUy/Py).

mcq.s: With fixed demand and an increase in supply, the price of the commodity is likely to:
mcq.x: If demand stays the same and supply rises, the excess supply pushes the equilibrium price down.

mcq.s: For pricing of public goods, the concept of 'shadow prices' was given by:
mcq.x: Jan Tinbergen defined shadow prices as the intrinsic (equilibrium) values of factors and products, used in social cost-benefit analysis.

mcq.s: Which of the following is NOT a public good?
mcq.x: Public goods are non-rival and non-excludable, like defence, administration and roads; cars are private goods.

mcq.s: If a commodity is provided free to the public by the Government, then:
o: the opportunity cost is transferred from the consumers of the product to the tax-paying public
the opportunity cost is transferred from the consumers of the product to the Government
mcq.x: Free goods still use resources; their cost is borne by taxpayers, so the opportunity cost shifts from the consumers to the tax-paying public.
